questions.positioning_one_line: In one or two sentences, how would you describe what you do, and for whom, to someone who has never heard of you?
questions.positioning_different: What do you do differently from the other options a customer could pick, and why does that matter to them?
questions.positioning_not_for: Who is your product not for? Which kinds of customer do you turn away or steer elsewhere?
questions.capability_core: What are the two or three things your product does that customers rely on most?
questions.capability_underrated: What can your product do that customers often don't realise until they've been using it for a while?
questions.capability_recent: What is the most useful thing you've shipped or improved recently, and what does it let a customer do now?
questions.pricing_model: How do you charge, and what does a typical customer pay? Share whatever you're comfortable saying publicly.
questions.pricing_who_pays: Who usually decides to pay for your product, and who uses it day to day?
questions.pricing_change: Has how you price changed, or is it about to? What would you want customers to understand about why?
questions.competitor_alternatives: What do customers use or do today instead of your product, including doing nothing?
questions.competitor_switch: When customers switch to you from something else, what usually made them switch?
questions.competitor_wrong: What do people get wrong about how you compare with the alternatives?
questions.problem_before: What is a customer's situation like just before they find you? What is going wrong for them?
questions.problem_cost: What does that problem cost them in time, money or stress? Use their numbers or words if you have them.
questions.problem_workaround: What workaround do customers put up with before they find you?
questions.objection_lost_deal: Think of a deal or signup you lost. What reason did the person give, or what do you think it really was?
questions.objection_hesitation: What makes people hesitate before they buy or start a trial?
questions.objection_answer: For the objection you hear most, what do you say that actually settles it?
questions.question_first_call: What are the first questions people ask when they talk to you or your team?
questions.question_repeated: Which question do you find yourself answering again and again?
questions.question_misunderstood: What do people commonly misunderstand about your product until someone explains it?
questions.trigger_moment: What moment makes someone start looking for a product like yours?
questions.trigger_event: What event in a customer's business, such as a hire, a launch or a deadline, tends to lead them to you?
questions.trigger_search: When customers first go looking, what words do they use to describe what they need?
questions.quote_customer_words: Is there something a customer said about the problem or about you that you keep coming back to? Paste it as they said it.
questions.quote_praise: What is the nicest thing a customer has said about you, in their own words? Only share it if they were happy for it to be used.
questions.quote_review: Is there a review, message or testimonial you are proud of? Paste the part that matters, as written.
questions.case_study_win: Tell us about a customer who got a clear result with you. Who were they and what happened?
questions.case_study_before_after: For one customer, what was the situation before and what is it now?
questions.case_study_surprise: Has a customer used your product in a way you did not expect? What did they do?
questions.usage_data_number: What is a real number about your product or customers that you would be happy to publish, and where does it come from?
questions.usage_data_trend: What has clearly changed in how customers use your product over the last year?
questions.usage_data_behaviour: What do your most successful customers do differently from the rest?

why.positioning: Positioning is how every post frames who you are and who you are for. Your own words keep it consistent.
why.capability: Posts stay accurate when they describe what your product really does, so we ask you rather than guess.
why.pricing: Pricing claims are risky to invent. We only write about it the way you say it.
why.competitor: How you compare with the alternatives shapes how carefully we word anything competitive.
why.problem: Posts land when they start from the problem your customers actually have, in the terms they use.
why.objection: The reasons people hesitate rarely appear in what you have already published, so only you can tell us.
why.question: Repeated questions are ready-made post topics that people are already asking about.
why.trigger: Knowing what sets someone off looking lets posts meet them at the right moment.
why.quote: Real customer words are the strongest proof. They are only ever used with your permission.
why.case_study: A concrete customer story gives posts something specific to point to.
why.usage_data: Real numbers make posts credible. We use only the ones you give us.
